canvasOwnership.whyNotTheSharedGuard: shared/canvas-owner.mjs assertOwnCanvas() answers 'is the canvas painting OUR PROBE page', because its callers write into a throwaway page. This task must modify MAIN itself, so the question is inverted: 'is the canvas painting MAIN'. openDocument() is documented not to switch tabs, so steering a probe and back would be a proof of nothing.
canvasOwnership.method: content identity of the painted document: active page uuid = MAIN, and the document the canvas paints returns 39 texts / 21 components / 55 wires / 2 pages, with text31 content = the 29-char project id. A different or empty page cannot produce that signature.
canvasOwnership.savePath: shared/page-cleanup.mjs saveOwnDocument() refuses probe===main by design (REFUSED_TARGET_IS_MAIN). The save was therefore eda.sch_Document.save() directly, gated by the identity check plus an exact read-back before the call.

conversion.unitTrap: TWO different conventions exist and they are not interchangeable. For sch_PrimitiveAttribute, modify() takes inches and the stored 0.01-inch value must be divided by 100 (doc section 14.22 item 3). For sch_PrimitiveText, modify('text31', {fontSize: X}) round-trips X unchanged: X=0.14 read back 0.14, so the text API takes the SAME unit getState_FontSize returns. Writing 0.14 would have shrunk the label by 100x.
conversion.evidence: r4t1-d1-write.json step 'modify-id target/100' read back fs=0.14, which is how the unit was settled without guessing.

calls.shapeBugFound: the first attempt passed the primitive OBJECT as the first argument. The implementation publishes {primitiveId: t, ...} with t used verbatim, so the object became '[object Object]' and the call silently did nothing (read-back stayed 16). Passing the id string is the working shape.
